wikipedia.extract: The Cape eagle-owl (Bubo capensis) is a species of owl in the family Strigidae. It is one of several large species of the eagle-owl genus Bubo.
wikipedia.title: Cape eagle-owl

wikipedia.extract: Bilateria () is a large clade of animals characterised by bilateral symmetry during embryonic development. This means their body plans are laid around a longitudinal axis with a front (or "head") and a rear (or "tail") end, as well as a left–right–symmetrical belly (ventral) and back (dorsal) surface.
wikipedia.title: Bilateria

wikipedia.extract: The austral snipes, also known as the New Zealand snipes or tutukiwi, are a genus, Coenocorypha, of tiny birds in the sandpiper family, which are now only found on New Zealand's outlying islands. There are currently three living species and six known extinct species, with the Subantarctic snipe having three subspecies, including the Campbell Island snipe discovered as recently as 1997.
wikipedia.title: Austral snipe

wikipedia.extract: Galloperdix is a genus of three species of bird in the pheasant family, Phasianidae. These terrestrial birds are restricted to the Indian subcontinent, with the red spurfowl and painted spurfowl in forest and scrub in India, and the Sri Lanka spurfowl in forests of Sri Lanka.
wikipedia.title: Galloperdix

wikipedia.extract: Collocalia is a genus of swifts, containing some of the smaller species termed "swiftlets". Formerly a catch-all genus for these, a number of its former members are now normally (though not by all authors) placed in Aerodramus.
wikipedia.title: Collocalia

wikipedia.extract: The dwarf lemurs are the lemurs of the genus Cheirogaleus. All of the species in this genus, like all other lemurs, are native to Madagascar.
wikipedia.title: Dwarf lemur

wikipedia.extract: Phoenicopterus is a genus of birds in the flamingo family Phoenicopteridae.
wikipedia.title: Phoenicopterus

commonNames.name: Australian Owlet-nightjar
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The Australian owlet-nightjar (Aegotheles cristatus) is a nocturnal bird found in open woodland across Australia and in southern New Guinea. It is the smallest nocturnal bird found in Australia, making it prone to predation.
wikipedia.title: Australian owlet-nightjar

wikipedia.extract: François' langur (Trachypithecus francoisi), also known as Francois' leaf monkey, the Tonkin leaf monkey, or the white side-burned black langur is a species of Old World monkey and the type species of its species group. It is one of the least studied of the species belonging to the Colobinae subfamily.
wikipedia.title: François' langur

wikipedia.extract: The banded stilt (Cladorhynchus leucocephalus) is a wader of the stilt and avocet family, Recurvirostridae, native to Australia. It belongs to the monotypic genus Cladorhynchus.
wikipedia.title: Banded stilt

commonNames.name: Drill
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The drill (Mandrillus leucophaeus) is a primate of the family Cercopithecidae (Old World monkeys), related to baboons and even more closely to the mandrill. The average wild drill has a lifespan of 20 years.
wikipedia.title: Drill (animal)

commonNames.name: Black Lemur
commonNames.source: The IUCN Red List of Threatened Species

wikipedia.extract: The black lemur (Eulemur macaco) is a species of lemur from the family Lemuridae. Like all lemurs, it is endemic to Madagascar.
wikipedia.title: Black lemur

wikipedia.extract: Gallirex is a genus of African birds in the family Musophagidae.
wikipedia.title: Gallirex

wikipedia.extract: Actitis is a small genus of waders, comprising two similar bird species.
wikipedia.title: Actitis

wikipedia.extract: Hydropsalis is a genus of nightjars in the family Caprimulgidae. The species are widely distributed across the tropical and subtropical regions of the New World.
wikipedia.title: Hydropsalis

wikipedia.extract: Aramidae is a bird family in the order Gruiformes. The limpkin (Aramus guarauna) is the only living member of this family, although other species are known from the fossil record, such as Papulavis annae from the Eocene of France, Aramus paludigrus from the Middle Miocene of Colombia and Badistornis aramus from the Oligocene of South Dakota, USA. Another Oligocene fossil from Europe, Parvigrus pohli, has been described as a mosaic of the features shared by the limpkins and the cranes.
wikipedia.title: Aramidae

gbif.scientificName: Eleoscytalopus G.N.Mauricio, Mata, Bornschein, C.D.Cadena, H.Alvarenga & Bonatto, 2008

wikipedia.extract: Eleoscytalopus is a genus of tapaculos found in lowland Atlantic forest of eastern Brazil. Until recently, they were included in the genus Scytalopus, but the two species are actually closer to the bristlefronts (genus Merulaxis).
wikipedia.title: Eleoscytalopus

gbif.scientificName: Homo antecessor Bermúdez de Castro et al., 1997

wikipedia.extract: Homo antecessor (Latin for 'pioneer man') is an extinct species of archaic human recorded in the Spanish Sierra de Atapuerca, a productive archaeological site, from 1.2 to 0.8 million years ago during the Early Pleistocene. Populations of this species may have been present elsewhere in Western Europe, and were among the first to settle that region of the world, hence the name.
wikipedia.title: Homo antecessor

wikipedia.extract: Telmabates is an extinct genus of presbyornithid bird from the Eocene Bird Clay Locality of the Sarmiento Formation of Chubut Province, Argentina. The genus contains a single species, T. antiquus.
wikipedia.title: Telmabates
